thread:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency breach detected for canary deployment 'v12' in us-west1. p99=6.2s (SLO 1.5s). Streaming stalls observed, ~18% of in-flight streams timed out. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/latency-canary
oncall-bot: Pager sent to oncall (ashley). See runbook: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/canary-latency

ashley (sre): Ack. Paging in. I'm looking at the canary dashboard, traces show a latency cluster at encoder shard 3. First hypothesis: kv-cache thrash + increased sequence lengths from new prompts.

miguel (infra): I see increased CPU steal on the GPU hosts for that shard, and OOM kill attempts on the encoder container around the same time. Logs show repeated eviction warnings.

sophia (runtime): v12 changed KV cache eviction policy (LRU window shrink). That could make smaller KV hit rates -> more recompute. Also the new attention kernel fallback path is used for long sequences.

ashley (sre): Quick mitigation options: 1) reduce canary weight to 0% (traffic shift), 2) route canary traffic to fallback model v11, 3) scale encoder pool + bump pod resources. Which is fastest?

miguel (infra): We can scale up encoders in us-west1 now, but image build for v12 is pinned. Scaling helps but may not fix algorithmic cache change. We can flip canary traffic weight to 0 in the control-plane in ~30s.

sophia (runtime): Routing to v11 is safe; v11 is compatible. If we flip weight to 0, that buys time for deeper triage. Recommend immediate traffic shift + lower retry budgets to reduce queueing.

karim (product): Heads up — a handful of customers on canary (alpha) might see degraded experience if we rollback or shift. Is there a CS churn risk?

emily (cs): I'm on standby. If we do a rollback I'll prepare a short note for the affected customers and open a support ticket list. No high-ARPU customers currently on canary, mostly early access.

ashley (sre): Action: shifting canary weight to 0 now. Miguel, can you run the control-plane command? I'll monitor p99 and streaming success.

miguel (infra): Running control-plane mutation: 
```
redwoodctl traffic set --deployment canary-v12 --region us-west1 --weight 0
```
Applied. Confirmed: weight=0 -> 0.0%

ashley (sre): Observing metrics... p99 dropped to 1.6s within 45s, streaming stalls down to 2.5%. Still above SLO but much improved. :thumbsup:

sophia (runtime): Good. Capture traces for the failure window: trace IDs start with 8f3a... I'll export the candidate traces and core dumps if any. Also check kv cache metrics for hit/miss ratio.

miguel (infra): No new OOMs after traffic shift. Encoder shard CPU/power consumption returned to baseline. Looks like traffic weight was the main driver.

ashley (sre): Proceeding to set temporary mitigation: keep canary weight at 0, scale encoder pool +2 replicas (safety), and tag the canary deployment as "paused".

sophia (runtime): I'm rolling a small patch to disable the new LRU window shrink flag on v12 image in staging, but that's not applicable to production until we ship v12-rollback image. For now, keep v12 traffic gated.

karim (product): Do we need to inform any external partners? Any customer-visible incident besides streaming stalls?

emily (cs): Opening support ticket for alpha cohort, sending canned message: "We're investigating increased tail latency for canary models; we've shifted affected traffic and will follow up with timeline." Will post updates on the alpha slack channel.

ashley (sre): Incident severity: S2 (SLO breach for non-prod canary causing degraded streaming for alpha users). No major customer outages. Assigning post-incident triage to runtime and infra teams.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3279. Page escalation window set to 30m.

sophia (runtime): Triage checklist: 1) Collect kv cache hit/miss timeline 2) Compare kernel selection metrics between v11/v12 3) Reproduce with synthetic long-sequence traces 4) Validate eviction policy params.

miguel (infra): I'll snapshot host metrics and kernel messages. Sharing temp link to logs: https://logs.redwood/ingest/stream/8f3a-traces

ashley (sre): Timeline notes: 00:00 alert -> 00:30 traffic shift -> 00:45 p99 near-SLO. Keeping incident open for postmortem data collection.

karim (product): Please capture the canary rollout config (traffic ramp config + any AB flags). We'll need to revisit rollout policy thresholds.

sophia (runtime): FYI the v12 rollout used a progressive ramp: 0.5% -> 2% -> 5% over 6h. Eviction flag changed in model-serving code in v12. That plus a small sample of long prompts looks to have triggered thrash.

emily (cs): I'll notify the alpha slack and the small set of trial customers that we've paused the canary and are investigating. Template ready.

ashley (sre): Handoff: I'm documenting live mitigation steps in the incident channel and will hand to the follow-the-sun oncall in ~25m. Action items:
- sophia: export traces + kv cache metrics (done by 12:30 UTC)
- miguel: host snapshots + OOM logs (12:30 UTC)
- emily: customer comms posted (12:15 UTC)
- karim: review rollout policy and patch plan (later today)

sophia (runtime): Exported traces: https://traces.redwood/8f3a/export (s3). KV metrics attached to incident.

miguel (infra): Host snapshot uploaded: https://artifacts.redwood/enc-shard3/snapshot.tgz

emily (cs): Customer message posted to #alpha-feedback. No negative responses so far.

ashley (sre): Closing real-time mitigation. Keeping incident open for full RCA. If anyone sees a re-occurrence, re-ping on this thread and I'll re-open page.

oncall-bot: Incident status updated -> mitigated. Assigned to: runtime + infra for RCA.

sophia (runtime): Preliminary root cause hypothesis: v12 changed eviction policy + attention kernel fallback under long sequences -> increased recompute and cache churn leading to encoder CPU pressure -> p99 latency spike.

miguel (infra): Agreed. Next steps: reproduce in staging with same config, add stronger guardrails to rollout (smaller ramp, autoscale thresholds, canary abort on p99 >2s), and prepare a v12 rollback candidate with eviction flag off.

karim (product): Add rollout policy change to roadmap. Also propose a safety gate: abort canary ramp if streaming success < 99.5% for 10m.

emily (cs): I'll prepare a concise post to customers summarizing action and ETA for RCA.

ashley (sre): Thanks team. Documenting incident notes and assigning RCA owners. Will file a postmortem draft under /postmortems/INC-2026-3279. :white_check_mark:

sophia (runtime): Follow-up: exporting a small repro harness and test vectors to the infra team.

miguel (infra): Received. Will run synthetic load tomorrow and verify autoscale reactions.

ashley (sre): Handoff complete. Oncall stepping down.

emily (cs): Closing loop with customers after RCA.

oncall-bot: Incident closed (mitigated -> monitoring).
